title: Does generic-gate cell count rank accelerator designs like SKY130-mapped area and clock period?
summary: The 40 MAC-engine designs of eda-harness (1–8 lanes, 4–8 bits) were mapped to the SKY130 HD standard-cell library (Yosys 0.33, ABC dc2; map, flip-flops mapped with dfflibmap, tt 25 °C 1.80 V liberty at a pinned ORFS commit). Generic-gate cell count ranks mapped area almost perfectly (Spearman 0.995, Kendall 0.954; 6.4–8.4 µm² per generic cell), but logic depth ranks ABC's mapped critical-path delay only at Spearman 0.611. So the (cells, cycles) Pareto front is identical to the (area, cycles) front, yet adding clock period moves it: with latency = cycles × delay, one of four generic-front designs drops off and a 5-bit design joins; top-5 overlap on the combined objective is 0.60. Limits: one design family, one ABC script, unconstrained map delay with no wires or placement, no place and route (not installed), so none of it is sign-off or silicon.
lede: the 40 MAC-engine designs mapped to the SKY130 HD cell library: generic cell count ranks mapped area at Spearman 0.995 but logic depth ranks mapped delay at only 0.611, so the (area, cycles) Pareto front is unchanged while the (area, latency) front loses one design and gains another.
